questions.q: What prompts Theo to check the AWS S3 backup bucket in this lesson?
options: An AWS billing alert
A customer-reported data leak
Nothing specific — it's a natural extension of the same review pass that caught the autoscaling issue
The replication job from Lesson 7 failed
questions.explain: No alert or complaint triggered this; it's good practice to review everything that shipped in the same window, not just the part that cost money.

questions.q: What does the bucket's Permissions tab show?
options: Public access: Blocked
Public access: Not blocked, with a warning that objects can be public
No permissions are configured at all
Access is restricted to Azure only
questions.explain: The 'Public access: Not blocked' banner, paired with 'Objects can be public,' is AWS directly flagging the exposure.

questions.q: What does the bucket policy's `"Principal": "*"` actually mean?
options: Only Driftwood's own AWS account can access the bucket
Only the designated backup-writer IAM role can access the bucket
Anyone, including people outside Driftwood's AWS account entirely, can access the bucket's objects
Access requires multi-factor authentication
questions.explain: A wildcard Principal applies to anyone, not just Driftwood's account or the intended replication role — the classic cause of accidental public exposure.

questions.q: What was the bucket policy supposed to grant access to instead?
options: The entire internet, by design
Only the specific IAM role used by the Lesson 7 cross-cloud replication job, driftwood-backup-writer
Only Priya Suresh's personal AWS login
No one — the bucket should have had no access at all
questions.explain: The intent was a single named principal, the replication job's IAM role — not a wildcard open to anyone.

questions.q: Why did this mistake go unnoticed for so long?
options: AWS does not provide any way to check bucket permissions
The bucket worked perfectly for its intended purpose the whole time, with no error or failed health check to call attention to the overly broad policy
The bucket was deleted and recreated multiple times
It was intentionally hidden by the replication job
questions.explain: Nothing breaks when a bucket is too permissive — the replication job still works fine, which is exactly why this kind of mistake can survive undetected.
